verdict: Uber grew revenue 20% to $12.0B in its strongest quarter ever, with operating profit of $770M — and a $6.4B one-off tax benefit then swelled net income to $6.9B.

follow100Note: Of the $57.71 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $57.56 accrued to Uber shareholders and $0.15 to non-controlling partners. The huge tax-benefit row is the one-off valuation-allowance release described below. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The strongest quarter yet
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 20% to $12.0B as trips rose 18% to 3.1 billion and Gross Bookings 18% to $44.2B. Mobility revenue jumped 25% and Delivery 21%; Freight was flat.

takeaways.title: Operating profit kept compounding
takeaways.text: Income from operations rose 18% to $770M, and Adjusted EBITDA jumped 44% to $1.8B — 4.2% of Gross Bookings, up from 3.4% a year ago. Operating cash flow was $1.8B and free cash flow $1.7B.

takeaways.title: A paper tax benefit stole the headline
takeaways.text: Net income of $6.9B is not money Uber earned selling rides: releasing a $6.4B tax valuation allowance — plus $556M of investment revaluation gains — did the heavy lifting. Costs also jumped: G&A hit $1,114M on legal and regulatory reserve charges.

oneTimers: Income taxes were a $6,002M benefit, not a bill — dominated by a $6.4B release of the valuation allowance on Uber's deferred tax assets, a non-cash accounting move reflecting that Uber now expects to use those past losses against future profits.
Net income includes a $556M pre-tax benefit from net unrealized gains on the revaluation of Uber's equity investments.

General & administrative expense jumped to $1,114M from $603M a year ago, including roughly $462M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve charges and settlements that Uber excludes from its non-GAAP figures.
otherDetail: Other income, net of $256M — including a $556M pre-tax gain from revaluing Uber's equity investments, partly offset by other items — less $117M of interest expense and a $10M loss from equity method investments.
footerNote: Net income of $6,901M includes $18M attributable to non-controlling interests; $6,883M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $3.21 EPS figure). Because the tax line is a benefit, the chart draws it as a green source flowing into net profit rather than as a tax bill.
